If a plurality is forming on you, still abstain and let the abstain bloc block it, since a counter-vote would not change the tally.

lesson_situation: The illusionist, holding one conceal, must decide whether tonight's pack victim is worth hiding. The wolf carrier has proposed a target who is pressing hardest for watch and follow claims. Day 2 ended with every living player abstaining, so no one has been eliminated and the town has no verified night results. Players are asking watch and follow holders to state who visited them, which would expose any uncovered visit. Information landscape: Information-starved. The only hard public facts are the first night's kill and concealment of player_1, and the healer save on player_5. Everything else is unverified claims about visits and roles. Stakes: With five eliminations needed before the leading evil faction can win, the board is far from decided, but the one remaining conceal is the illusionist's last chance to shield a kill from the town's watch and follow roles. Spending it on a victim whose trace would expose the pack, or wasting it on a low-value victim, both narrow the pack's cover for the rest of the game. Forward exposure: Spending the remaining conceal on tonight's pack victim would hide that victim's role and trace from the town's watch and follow roles, committing the illusionist to a hidden body that cannot be reversed; declining keeps the conceal but leaves the victim's role and any visits to them readable by a watcher or follower. Target landscape: Nine living players are candidates for the pack's kill, with no public role claims among the living that the town has verified. The carrier for tonight is the other wolf, who has proposed a target among the most active information-seekers in the day discussion. One earlier victim, player_1, was killed and concealed, so their role is known only to the illusionist.
lesson_action: If you conceal, carry the kill yourself, because then you leave no trace at that door and the carrier's visit is hidden from a Sentinel watching the victim or a Trailseer following the carrier. If a Sigilist with sigils left is alive or likely, or it is not your turn to carry, let the pack's kill go unconcealed instead of visiting the body as a non-carrier. A non-carrier's visit to hide the body stays visible to a watcher on that door, and a carrier's attack can be punished by a sigil.

Stakes: Six alive with four eliminations until the leading evil faction can win at worst for the town; the concealed body's side is unknown, so one more elimination could decide the game under at least one way that side could fall. A wrong lynch or an unhidden kill that exposes the pack is costly, while the single remaining conceal is the only tool left to protect a victim's role from the town. Forward exposure: Spending the last conceal on tonight's victim would make the victim's role hidden until game end, so the town cannot read that role or its record, and the conceal leaves no trace at the victim's door; a visible vote push on a claimed role would commit the illusionist's public stance and is hard to reverse once the village has acted on it. Two claim roles: one player claims Sigilist (a no-effect sigil on another claimant), one claims Investigator (a Not suspicious check on a player who died as a concealed speculator) and a Sentinel claim and a Trailseer claim also stand. Keep the last conceal for the kill where that traceless result matters most.
